newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks hold ground in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks hold ground in quiet trade.

text.p: The Australian stock market held on to a small gain all afternoon to the close on Wednesday, with little fresh news to drive a six-week rally to higher levels.
The All Ordinaries Index pushed up about 10 points in late morning trade, but soon settled back to end the day 2.3 points higher at 2,615.9 in quiet trade.
"For the next few days there doesn't seem to be anything around the corner that will drive the market aggressively higher," said David Iron, head of institutional sales at HSBC James Capel Australia.

Brokers said the possibility of a further official interest rate cut, which boosted the market on Friday and Monday, appeared to have eased with the release of moderately strong gross domestic product data for the March quarter.
Weaker commodity prices have also taken some of the gloss off the resources sector, with the mining index coming back about 0.4 percent on the day.

Coke bottler Coca-Cola Amatil posted a strong gain after announcing it had reached final agreement on a share swap deal with San Miguel Corp to acquire the Philippine group's soft drink operations. C-C Amatil closed on its highs at A$16.10 (US$12.24), up 70 cents.
Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) traded 18.9 million shares to top turnover after going ex a 22 cent interim dividend, closing down 24 cents at A$8.88.
Among other banks, the Commonwealth Bank of Australia retraced recent losses to add 31 cents to A$14.27, while the other two big banks were slightly firmer.

Queensland's so-called Rundle twins, Central Pacific Minerals and Southern Pacific Petroleum, each rose about 13 percent after announcing a deal with financiers to proceed with stage one of the long-mooted Stuart shale oil deposit development.
In the building sector, James Hardie continued its recent run adding another five cents to A$4.20 ahead of the release of its annual results on Thursday.
Bellwether Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd partly retraced Tuesday's decline, adding 10 cents to A$18.97, while News Ltd fell 15 cents to A$5.71.
